en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Cittāgāra Vagga 49.
The Training Rule on Mastering Animal Sciences.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs were studying secular lore.
People criticized, complained, and spread it about:
"How can these bhikkhunīs study secular lore? They are just like householders who enjoy sensual pleasures!"
The bhikkhunīs heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires... [and so on]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
"How can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six master such worldly lore?"... [and so on]...
“Is it true, monks, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs are mastering ‘animal sciences’?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them … [as before] …
"How indeed, monks, can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs master secular lore?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of those with faith...

And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: "Whatever bhikkhunī should master secular lore, there is an offense of expiation."* (*The full rule includes the penalty of forfeiture and confession.)"
“Whatever nun should master secular lore, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya). “Whatever nun” means whichever nun of such a kind...
[and so forth].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Low arts" (tiracchānavijjā) means:
"Whatever external [teaching] is unbeneficial.
"Should master it":
by mastering it word by word, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya) for every word.
If she masters it syllable by syllable, there is an offense of expiation for each syllable.
There is no offense if she is mastering writing.
One masters it for the sake of retention;
one masters a protective chant for the sake of guarding oneself;
[or] for one who is insane.
"For one who is a first-offender.
The ninth training rule is concluded.
